title: Runbook: PAC file, explicit proxy and DPP outages, PAC causes and authentication loops

prose.label: PAC causes.
prose.text: {{manual-proxy-test}} {{parsing-direct}} {{audit-and-revert}} WinMTR collection for PAC is in [[zia.traffic-forwarding.runbook.tunnel-path]].

reachability-hosts.statement: In the runbook's section on troubleshooting Zscaler public DC issues, in an internet-down situation with PAC, the runbook says to validate DNS resolution and connectivity for pac.<cloudname>.net, login.<cloudname>.net, gateway.<cloudname>.net and the authentication server, on 80/443/DPP using ping and Telnet.

quotes: The following sections describe how to troubleshoot Zscaler public DC issues.
For PAC, validate the successful DNS resolution and connectivity for the following:
pac.<cloudname>.net
login.<cloudname>.net
gateway.<cloudname>.net
Authentication server (IP FQDN)
Validate the connection on 80/443/DPP, using ping and Telnet tools to validate the connection.

dpp-telnet-expected.statement: The runbook lists a failed Telnet to DPP (its example port is 10938) as 'not provisioned', alongside a successful Telnet to port 80/443.

quotes: Failed TELNET (DPP 10938) - not provisioned
Successful TELNET (port 80/443)

powershell-alternative.statement: When the Telnet client is not enabled and the end device has restrictive permissions, the runbook says PowerShell can be used to check network reachability.

quotes: In case the Telnet client is not enabled, and the end device has restrictive permissions, you can use PowerShell to check the network reachability.

download-pac.statement: The runbook says to copy the PAC URL from the Admin Console and confirm the affected device can download the PAC file; if it can, open the file to identify the primary and secondary data center and run ping and Telnet reachability tests towards both.

quotes: copy the PAC URL from the Zscaler Admin Console and confirm if the impacted user device can download the PAC file successfully.
open the downloaded PAC file to identify the primary and secondary DC. Run reachability tests (ping and Telnet) towards the primary and secondary DC.

fragmentation.statement: If the device cannot download the PAC file although pac.<cloudname>.net is reachable, the runbook says to run a client packet capture and check for IP fragmentation; the filter icmp.type==3 and icmp.code==4 indicates a fragmentation issue and the Wireshark filter ip.flags.mf == 1 shows all fragmented packets.

quotes: If user device is unable to download the PAC file, although reachability to pac.<cloudname>.net is present, run the client's packet capture and validate that there is no IP fragmentation taking place.
The filter that indicates a fragmentation issue is:
icmp.type==3 and icmp.code==4
To look for all fragmented packets, use the Wireshark filter:
ip.flags.mf == 1

avoid-fragmentation.statement: The runbook says to determine the IP packet size the network supports, using Path MTU discovery or setting the Maximum Segment Size (MSS), to avoid IP fragmentation.

quotes: In order to avoid IP fragmentation, determine the size of the IP packets that the network supports. There are two approaches that are generally used: Path MTU discovery and Setting Maximum Segment Size (MSS).

manual-proxy-test.statement: To test whether an issue is PAC-related, the runbook says to find the data center the customer is connected to at http://ip.zscaler.com, log out of Client Connector, take the FQDN of the PAC VIP for the DC from config.zscaler.com, set it as a manual proxy on port 80/443 with the relevant IdP authentication domains in the bypass, and visit an HTTP site; if the test page loads, troubleshooting focuses on the PAC file.

quotes: Perform a test with a manual proxy to confirm if the issue is PAC-related.
Go to http://ip.zscaler.com to find the DC the customer is connected to.
Log out of Zscaler Client Connector, then go to https://config.zscaler.com to find the FQDN of PAC VIP for the DC.
set a manual proxy server to the FQDN of the DC, with port 80/443. Add the relevant IdP authentication domains in the proxy bypass.
If the test page loads, focus your troubleshooting on the PAC file.
Visit an HTTP website (e.g., http://isitfridayyet.net) to complete the Zscaler cookie authentication process.

parsing-direct.statement: The runbook says a PAC parsing issue could cause applications to send traffic direct, which might drop at the customer firewall.

quotes: PAC parsing issue could cause applications to send traffic direct which might drop at the customer firewall.

audit-and-revert.statement: To check for recent PAC changes the runbook points to Administration > Admin Management > Audit Logs with the PAC File Sub-Category filter; to revert, open Hosted PAC Files, Manage Versions, then Actions > Deploy on the previous version. A PAC-only scenario needs the browser cache cleared and might need a browser restart.

quotes: go to Administration > Admin Management > Audit Logs and select the PAC File Sub-Category drop-down menu.
go to Infrastructure > Internet & SaaS > Traffic Forwarding > Traffic Steering > Hosted PAC Files.
Find the relevant PAC file, and click Manage Versions.
Click Actions and select Deploy to revert the changes to the previous PAC version.
For a PAC-only scenario, a browser cache must be cleared, and a browser restart might be required.

auth-loop.statement: The runbook describes an authentication loop that can occur when the IdP request is both forwarded via Internet & SaaS and redirected for authentication; it is identified in a packet capture or browser trace by a 307 redirection for an IdP request.

quotes: An authentication loop could happen if the request for IdP is configured to be forwarded via Internet & SaaS, and the request for IdP is also redirected for authentication, causing an endless loop.
take a packet capture or browser trace and look for a 307 redirection for an IdP request.

auth-loop-fix.statement: Zscaler recommends bypassing IdP traffic from forwarding to Internet & SaaS, or at least configuring it in Authentication Exemptions; the runbook says to add a bypass for the authentication domain in the PAC file or add the domains under Administration > Advance Settings > Authentication Exemptions.

quotes: Zscaler recommends bypassing IdP traffic from forwarding to Internet & SaaS, or at least ensuring that the IdP traffic is configured in Authentication Exemptions.
Add a bypass for the authentication domain in the PAC file, or add the domains to the authentication bypass list, by going to Administration > Advance Settings > Authentication Exemptions.
